Two measured fixes were needed to get here:
  CLS 0.65 -> 0: filter chips are injected after the snapshot resolves and wrapped to a
    variable number of rows, pushing the list down 120px. Measured board top via
    tools/measure-empty.mjs (snapshot blocked) vs tools/measure.mjs (loaded):
    471px before data -> 474px after data = 3px shift. Fix: .chips{flex-wrap:nowrap;
    overflow-x:auto;min-height:28px} plus a non-wrapping result count.
  LCP 4.5s -> 2.6s: descriptions were 56% of a 668KB first payload. Split into a lean index
    (281KB) plus 4 details-*.json chunks fetched only when a task is opened.
  accessibility 96 -> 100: the `list` and `label-content-name-mismatch` audits failed
    because role="button" + aria-label were on the <li>, destroying list semantics. The
    <li> keeps its list role; the inner <button> carries the label.

The 780 KB of snapshot data (dist/snapshot.json + details-*.json) is omitted: the API caps a
delivery at 50,000 characters and the data alone is 16x that. It is also *fetched*, not
authored, and tools/fetch-snapshot.mjs is included - one command rebuilds all five files
byte-for-byte from the public API. tools/xss-test.mjs, shots.mjs, view-shots.mjs,
measure.mjs and measure-empty.mjs are likewise omitted for size; their real output is
quoted in full in the runs[] entries above rather than summarised.

design_notes:
The current board page is a table. Three deliberate changes, each argued by something measurable.

1. Rank by money, not by recency. 72 of 207 tasks carry a bounty and the rest pay nothing, but
   the default order buries that. A Bounty-down sort plus Paid/Free-only filters answers "where
   is the money" in one click, and settled payments get a first-class tab rather than a detail
   page: on a board where 44 payments totalling 5.30 USDC have actually settled, the hit rate is
   the interesting number, and the current board never shows it.

2. Status as a left edge, not a badge. A 3px colour rule on each card edge makes 207 tasks
   scannable as bands without reading a word. The status pill remains but is now redundant
   rather than load-bearing. Age moves to the right edge, so the eye reads what, then when,
   then who.

3. Descriptions are a resource, not a wall. Cards show a 260-char summary and full text loads
   on open. The old page renders every description inline: a wall of text with no entry point.
   The same split took LCP from 4.5s to 2.6s, so the affordance and the performance win are one
   decision rather than two.

Deliberately not done: no dark-only styling (both themes first-class, T toggles); no client-side
fetch to the live API, because it sends no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header and a browser
genuinely cannot read it. The app ships an honest build-time snapshot and says so in the
footer. A UI that presents yesterdays data as if it were live is worse than one that admits it
is a snapshot.
